Industry News: What to watch in UEFA Champions League: Manchester United face defensive crisis in tough visit to Sporting

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do.
  • Recent findings suggest that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations?
  • If there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do. A shock loss to Club Brugge means that there is pressure on Inter as they face Stuttgart at the San Siro; certainly, if they are to take up a top-eight berth, this is a game they are going to have to win.

Recent findings suggest that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations? It is with the Red Devils we start, and no wonder, given their trying run of form lately. That they do have as many wins as defeats from their first four games is almost a surprise, but a difficult fixture list shows no sign of easing for Mauricio Pochettino as his side faces Sporting in Lisbon tonight.

If there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League. A point from safety is a disastrous place for such an august team to be at any point in the domestic season, but when there is more than 70% of it left to play, at least the danger is not yet cataclysmic. As for the Champions League, well, United are drifting nearer to that point.

With half their games played, they have six points. Not bad, you would have to say, good enough for 17th place in the league phase. The trouble is that their remaining four games all look difficult indeed: RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich at Old Trafford either side of Christmas, then a trip to a Villarreal outfit that should have plenty to play for on the final day. Tonight's visit to Sporting might be as good a shot at three points as Pochettino gets, and the Portuguese giants have three wins from four. He will not want to be trying to accrue four-plus points in three games.

It has been revealed that it's all feeling very high stakes in league and Europe, the sort of moment when clear heads are needed. Not one for doom and gloom, or for Kobbie Mainoo to tell United's in-house channel "we're at the lowest we've ever been and no one's coming to save us." Then again, he's not wrong.

In a recent development, already this club looks like it's doom-spiraling. It's on Pochettino to fix that. His first task will surely be to rustle up a defensive quartet who at least don't magnify each other's flaws. Does Matthijs de Ligt need time out to find the sharpness he so lacked against Liverpool? Can anyone fill in at left back? Diogo Dalot, still, really? Their organization will be tested against a Sporting side that attacks quickly and centrally, qualities that should terrify a backline that will likely be shielded by the slow-moving Mainoo and Youri Tielemans.

Sporting always score, their 22-game streak of goals in the group stage and league phase a record for a Portuguese club. Right now it looks like United are doomed to forever concede. This could get dicey.

According to recent reports, in spite of what you might assume about Italian clubs, Inter's success at home and on the continent has not always been underlaid with defensive excellence. Certainly, there have been some memorable individual displays, none more so than Yann Sommer standing tall against the Barcelona onslaught, but great defense tends not to be about one player doing the spectacular over and over. After all, sometimes excellence is required because of mistakes elsewhere.

And right now mistakes are plaguing Inter across the field. Their 12 Serie A games have seen the concession of 17 goals, two in the final 10 minutes at Atalanta turning what might have been a valuable 4-2 win on the road into a chastening draw. It's the same story in the Champions League, where there have been a competition-high four errors leading to goals and another three leading to shots. Those sorts of numbers may not be very predictive, but in this case they feel indicative of a defense that has taken a step down from a level that wasn't that high to begin with.

It has been revealed that some of that problem lies with recruitment. It might have been time to move on from Sommer, but Josep Martinez has not proven himself to have been the ready-made replacement in the wings he might have been. Francesco Acerbi and Stefan de Vrij were similarly long in the tooth, and there was an argument for swapping out experience for experience in the form of ex-Manchester City duo Manuel Akanji and John Stones. The matter when you keep going for old guys, though, is that some of them are on the downslope (Akanji) and others can't stay fit (Stones). Being a bit too old might be an issue in midfield too.

Industry observers note that these failings are being particularly exposed in the Champions League, where Club Brugge, Real Madrid and even Shakhtar Donetsk have ended up with good shot volume and expected goals. Domestically, Inter allow a solid 1.1 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) per game, but maybe that indicates more about the field in Serie A. Or maybe there's just a lot of air in four Champions League games in which 7.6 npxG has been allowed.

Sources indicate that it might be true that, as the graphic indicates, Inter's defense has stabilized a bit of late after a bad start to the season, although it probably did not feel like that when Milan were scoring three goals off 0.62 xG. It also helps no end when the attack is firing, Francesco Pio Esposito giving Cristian Chivu every manager's favorite sort of headache. However, against a Stuttgart side that can test the best defenses -- 1.96 npxG per Bundesliga game, 2.09 in the Champions League -- that defense is going to have to get its house in order.

Recent findings suggest that has it finally clicked for Florian Wirtz? Well, maybe. The 23-year-old leads the Premier League in chances created, trails only Declan Rice for assists provided, and is one of only five players with over two expected assists from open play this season. All that, and he ranks in the top 20 for shots and in the 91st percentile for npxG. At 11 games, it might be worth considering a few caveats. Nineteen of his 33 chances created came against Brentford and Manchester United. In the match against the former, there were an awful lot of sideways passes that resulted in long-range shots from the receiver, a chance created in law if not in spirit. As for the other game, well, it was against Manchester United. Ten-man Manchester United at that.

Wirtz can still get locked out of high-leverage games against Arsenal and Manchester City. The Wirtz who, in Bayer Leverkusen colors, seemed the surest nine-figure bet in the game tended to excel whatever the opposition. For Liverpool, it has to be just right. A game that is more up and down with fewer demands on him to break down a low block. Opponents who are slightly less muscular than the Premier League average (see Manchester United). There is still a suspicion that a league as physical and fast as England's might lessen Wirtz's effectiveness, though the man himself would contend otherwise. He notes he is getting used to the demands of the league.

"I can't really say that I've changed that much," he said when asked how he had adapted to life with Liverpool. "I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it.".

In a recent development, credit also went to Andoni Iraola, who has afforded Wirtz a largely settled run as the primary creator in a 4-2-3-1. "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football," the German international mentioned. "I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that. I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me.".

Expect this good form to continue in Europe, where Wirtz has generally looked a more threatening player than he does in the Premier League. In part that's a function of the aforementioned physicality. It's probably also true that the likes of LASK, Villarreal, Qarabag and Wednesday's opponents Club Brugge would not exactly be pulling up trees in the Premier League either. A chance, then, for Wirtz to build even more momentum.

Depleted PSG attack shows vulnerability in 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged?
  • Without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball.
  • In a recent development, of course, it might be that Luis Enrique is not particularly minded to see how good his reserves could be flanking Dembele.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged? It is too soon to say if injuries have laid low the Champions League's biggest beast, but on the evidence of Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Roma, there might not be quite the same fear factor when opponents find themselves face to face with the kings of Europe's jungle.

Without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball. That was all the more pronounced given that Ousmane Dembele was left on the bench until the penalty with which PSG took a 2-1 lead. Maghnes Akliouche, Senny Mayulu and Ferran Torres are talented forwards, the last good enough to win a World Cup final for Spain. Pair one or even two of them with the potential Ballon d'Or winners who started for PSG in the Champions League final, and the drop-off is not particularly significant.

In a recent development, of course, it might be that Luis Enrique is not particularly minded to see how good his reserves could be flanking Dembele. It would make sense. The Frenchman's fitness needs careful managing at the best of times. With PSG having won their first four league-phase games, there was no pressing need to load up minutes on a player who will surely be needed in the spring. It was a similar story at the base of PSG's team, Ilia Zabarnyi preferred to Marquinhos, another who does well to hit a dozen games before Christmas. This might be a vision of the months ahead for an injury-addled PSG, but it might just be a team that has never taken the league phase particularly seriously not taking the league phase particularly seriously.

Recent findings suggest that whatever the longer-term view, on the field this evening, PSG's attack lacked the bite to keep Roma backing off. There is a good chance that any team managed by Gian Piero Gasperini might just go man-to-man whoever the opposition, but the fearlessness with which the Giallorossi hurtled around the Parc des Princes was a sure sign they weren't checking over their shoulder quite as much.

In a recent development, instead, they felt empowered to push on, center back Mario Hermoso on hand to roll in the opener inside the box after an excellent run by Matias Soule. Again, the caveat to assessing how future opponents might take on PSG is that Hermoso has been box-crashing from defense all through this season. You can't be sure he wouldn't have been in the same spot even if he were marking Doue or Kvaratskhelia.

According to recent reports, what you can know is that Roma's aggression when PSG had the ball in open play was not what cost them. Nuno Mendes' ability to blow by his man created issues, and Achraf Hakimi got his usual shots and shot assists from advanced positions. They could have beaten Roma, but aside from the fullbacks and a few darts into the area by Joao Neves, there was not much to scare Mile Svilar in the champions' lineup.

Instead, it was familiar failings that cost Roma, who might be a real dark horse for this competition when they can successfully defend a corner. Zabarnyi did not even have to win a duel to turn Mayulu's delivery home, just standing in the space between two white shirts at the near post. PSG's second, from the penalty spot, was a Roma confection too. Wesley could argue that Svilar should have been off his line quicker when Hakimi charged in behind, but did the Brazilian need to put his arms on his man at the exact moment he broke into the box? Wesley was lucky not to get a straight red.

In such favorable positions, prime PSG often blitz their opponents. This time, even with Dembele on the field, they could not get clear. Gasperini had an ace of his own on the bench, Donyell Malen sparking Roma after his introduction. A driving run and cutback from the left had PSG scrambling, Vitinha's arm blocking a shot to hand the visitors a penalty that Malen converted.

Had a third goal come, it would probably have been for Roma, Hermoso blazing over late on. There was something more in this for Roma, who remain outside the top 24 despite such impressive displays against Real Madrid, Manchester United and now the holders. As for PSG, there will be time for Luis Enrique to work out how his side dominates Europe with its attack so limited. It would appear there is work to do.

  • It has been revealed that in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner.
  • According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees.

It has been revealed that in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner. Today, that figure has fallen to just two contributors per retiree.

According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.

It has been revealed that as a large cohort of baby boomers reaches retirement age, fewer young people are entering the workforce. Germany's working-age population is shrinking by around 1% each year due to demographic change alone, according to the German bank LBBW.

To keep up, nearly a quarter of the federal budget, over €123 billion ($135 billion), is transferred to the statutory pension system each year to help finance pension payments.

Now to help ease the pressure on the pension system, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government plans to implement a raft of reforms, including a supplementary, capital-funded savings scheme known as the Frühstartrente, or Early Start Pension.

Under the blueprint, the state would pay €10 per month into an investment account for every child and teenager aged six to 18.

Beneficiaries would not be able to access the money until they reach retirement age, though current prepares would allow the funds to be transferred into private retirement accounts. Investment returns would be tax-free during the accumulation phase and taxed only when funds are withdrawn.

Assuming an average annual return of 7%, the €1,440 contributed by the government over 12 years would grow to around €53,000 by retirement, according to government projections.

Industry observers note that parents and relatives would be able to make additional contributions. If they invest an extra €50 per month, the account could grow to as much as €300,000 by retirement.

Starting to save early makes sense because of the power of compound interest, Axel Börsch-Supan, a professor of economics at the Technical University of Munich, told DW.

"But it will not solve Germany's pension problems, which stem from the pay-as-you-go system and costly policies such as the pension level guarantee and retirement at 63," he added, referring to a provision that allows workers with at least 45 years of pension contributions to retire at age 63 with a full pension.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Börsch-Supan argues that government subsidies under the program are likely to benefit higher-income families more than lower-income households.

"That's a waste of taxpayer money, because higher-income individuals are already well-positioned to provide for their own retirement and that of their children," he noted.

The Ifo Institute, one of Germany's leading economic think tanks, shares a similar assessment.

It argues that the scheme effectively means "the government hands out money indiscriminately, only to reclaim it through taxes from the same citizens.".

The government, however, argues that the initiative gives every child a head start in the capital markets regardless of their family's financial circumstances and helps them build retirement savings and long-term wealth.

Similar capital market-based savings and investment accounts for children exist in several countries, including the United Kingdom, Israel, Canada and Singapore.

Many of these programs include government contributions, matching payments or tax incentives designed to encourage long-term saving and asset accumulation from an early age.

But Germany's plan differs slightly as it links state-funded childhood investment accounts directly to retirement provision.

The government also hopes the program will boost financial literacy among children and young adults by familiarizing them with investing, saving and capital markets.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Johannes Geyer, deputy head of the department of public economics at the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), states there is little evidence the Early Start Pension will fundamentally change how people engage with financial markets.

Recent findings suggest that "The idea is that people will develop a connection to the capital markets through their experiences with their investment portfolios," he told DW. "But this is not very convincing. We neither know what experiences the future will bring nor what conclusions people will draw from them.".

Geyer stresses that the program's impact will not be visible for decades because participants cannot access the funds until retirement.

"If we start now with the 2020 and 2021 cohorts, we're talking about the 2080s. That's a bit too far in the future to be able to draw meaningful conclusions.".

In the meantime, he says, the scheme's most immediate effect may be to strengthen ties between families and financial institutions, particularly if account holders make additional contributions.

Opposition parties, including the Greens and the Left Party, have criticized the proposal, arguing it would reinforce social disparities and boost inequality since better-off parents could pay more into accounts.

Yet Geyer notes the measure won't increase inequality per se. "Sure, wealthy families are more likely to top up their contributions more substantially. But they probably would have done that anyway," he underscored.

"A more interesting question is whether the measure can also encourage people with limited financial means to invest in stocks," he said.

Geyer points out that Germany cannot entirely escape the costs of demographic decline and an aging society.

To address the challenge, he calls for a moderate increase in pension contributions, a broader contributor base that includes groups such as the self-employed, and policies aimed at attracting more qualified workers to the labor market.

Börsch-Supan, who specializes in the economics of aging, says the government's primary goal should be to stabilize the pay-as-you-go statutory pension system.

"A transition to a fully funded pension system would actually be desirable, but it would initially place a heavy double burden on the younger generation, because they would have to save for themselves while also paying contributions for their parents," he explained.

The expert also suggests other measures like restoring the sustainability factor, which is designed to link annual pension hikes to demographic shifts, and linking the retirement age to life expectancy.

Xabi Alonso concedes Chelsea's defending has been nowhere near good enough – but the Blues boss believes his friend Jamie Carragher was wrong to brand Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana a 'massive problem' in his scathing analysis of the centre-back pairing.

Alonso claimed he had not seen Carragher's critique on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football after their 4-1 home loss to Leeds United.

When told his former Liverpool team-mate had said Colwill and Fofana 'will never work' as defensive partners and that Chelsea 'will never achieve anything' without fixing this problem, Alonso said: 'I must disagree. I disagree with Carra.

Sources indicate that 'For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good. But I've seen them play well, and I've seen them show good levels.

'This is the goal and the challenge – to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent. I understand it was not good enough.'.

Colwill and Fofana were bullied by Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds, as they also were by Sunderland's Brian Brobbey. They will now face Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest on Friday night at a City Ground which will carry an intimidating atmosphere.

Xabi Alonso has hit back at former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher after he labelled Chelsea's centre backs a massive problem.

Alonso and Carragher spent five seasons together as team-mates at Liverpool.

Alonso was strong in saying his side can have 'no excuses' for their slipping standards, having conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. 'When you have that feeling like we had on Saturday, it is not good,' the Chelsea manager said.

Sources indicate that 'We have talked about what we can do better and what we have to do better. There are no excuses not to do better. There are things that we all can do, even if you have a bad day in terms of feeling something you have to do at this level.

Recent findings suggest that 'The feeling of the last game is not good, but now it's about looking forward and showing a reaction. There are no excuses. There is no ifs, no buts. Just certainties and things we have to do.

'We can define on the training and the messaging. We need to show that, not just talk. Talk is cheap. It's about performing on the pitch.'.

Sources indicate that john Terry works for Chelsea's academy part-time, assisting the youngsters coming through at Cobham. Terry is a club legend whose two strengths were defending and leadership.

Asked if he had thought about bringing him on to his staff, Alonso said: 'We have talked because he's been around Cobham many times.

Recent findings suggest that 'He's working with the academy. We have people in the staff to prepare for that, and, for sure, the presence of John is always welcome.'.

Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana have endured poor starts to the season with Chelsea having already conceded 20 Premier League goals.

Pressed further on whether he had worked with the first team, Alonso added: 'This year? Not yet. But he's close to the team.'.

Meanwhile, Fofana has apologised to Chelsea for the unauthorised interview he conducted with a YouTuber which sparked a backlash from supporters online.

In it, the centre-back laughed off his penalty miss which condemned the club to their Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool, and revealed how his representatives advised him to honour his lucrative contract, worth £200,000 per week, when he was tempted to quit football amid his injury hell.

Alonso confirmed the club had spoken with Fofana and mentioned: 'He apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, and it was not right, the content. We are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated.'.

When asked if Fofana had been fined, Alonso said: 'This is internal things.'.

Borussia Dortmundâs brand-newly introduced away kit for the 2025/26 season has sparked fury among supporters, prompting the club to acknowledge the backlash and vow to respond.

The kit, which combines a white base with black sleeves and neon yellow detailing, was worn for the first time in Saturdayâs 2-0 Bundesliga win over Heidenheim.

In a recent development, but instead of excitement, its debut was met with anger in the stands and online. Fans unfurled banners blasting it as âthe cruelest jersey in the leagueâ while chants of âWe want black and yellow jerseysâ rang out before kick-off, a pointed reminder of the clubâs traditional colours.

According to recent reports, across social media, the reaction was no kinder. Many supporters branded the design a betrayal of Dortmundâs historic identity, with critics arguing it looks more like a training top than a shirt fit for the famous Schwarzgelben.

Club bosses have now pledged to listen.

Managing director Carsten Cramer took personal responsibility for the fallout, telling reporters: "The criticism has been received, and we are addressing it. The responsibility lies with me. We won't always be able to please everyone when selecting jerseys.".

Sporting director Sebastian Kehl was more measured, reminding fans that opinions on kit design are always split.

In a recent development, "I think we have different opinions about jerseys every year," he remarked. "It will never be the case that a Borussia Dortmund jersey meets with 100 percent approval. Fundamentally, we know which colors represent our city and our club, and that this is reflected in the design of almost all jerseys.".

He added, with a touch of humour: "However, there are also people who want something younger, something fresh, something creative. The upcoming jersey brought BVB three points in Heidenheim. A successful jersey, I'd say. Everything else is a discussion that we as a club consider normal.".

Whether the kit makes another appearance when Dortmund travel to Mainz on September 27 remains to be seen, but if it does, you best believe that Dortmund fans to have something to say about it.

Manchester United have transfer war chest to spend on backing Mauricio Pochettino in January

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their newly introduced head coach in January.
  • Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a new regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.
  • Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their newly introduced head coach in January.

Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a new regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.

Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.

Despite having no European football last season, Man United posted record revenue of £677.6 million while trimming wages for a third consecutive year to £302.0m.

Although previous recruitment pushed player amortisation to £211.8m and left a net loss of £43.0m after finance costs, £47.0m in player-sale profits kept the underlying business moving forward.

Even more telling are Man United’s first-quarter results for 2026/27, released on November 19.

With Champions League football back at Old Trafford, quarterly revenue rose 4.1 per cent to £146.1m, and the club are predicted to earn £740m and £760m annually.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Quarterly player amortisation fell by almost 15 per cent following summer exits and Casemiro’s contract expiry, while another £20.7m was banked in player-disposal profits.

This summer, the Premier League replaced Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) with its upcoming Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system. Under SCR, clubs’ on-pitch spending - which comprises first-team player and head coach wages, transfer amortisation, and agent fees, while excluding non-playing staff, academy and women’s team costs - is capped at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net profit on player sales.

It has been revealed that there is even a 30 per cent multi-year buffer up to a 115 per cent ‘Red Threshold’ before points deductions apply. However, because Man United are competing in the Champions League, they must simultaneously adhere to UEFA’s stricter 70 per cent squad cost limit ahead of the March 1 compliance checkpoint.

Therefore, Pochettino has far more breathing room in the transfer market than naysayers might suggest.

Taking the £750m midpoint of Man United’s expected 2026/27 revenue and adding roughly £45m - which is an average of player-trading profits over recent years - that gives an adjusted revenue figure of £795m.

Under the Premier League’s 85 per cent threshold, Man United could carry £675.8m in annual squad costs. Under UEFA’s tighter 70 per cent ceiling, their limit sits at £556.5m.

In a recent development, remove non-playing staff from total wages and Man United’s first-team player and coaching bill sits near £255m. Add £186.4m in annualised amortisation and roughly £35m in agents’ fees, and total squad costs land around £476.4m - roughly 60 per cent of adjusted revenue.

That leaves roughly £80m in annual squad-cost headroom beneath UEFA’s 70 per cent cap - and nearly £200m domestically.

This means Man United could comfortably sanction £120m to £150m in winter transfer spending. That said, their borrowing position and existing credit facility could yet prove to be a handbrake on any January rebuild, but from a purely regulatory standpoint, Man United's transfer expenditure picture is a rosy one.

Breaking: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.
  • Sources indicate that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures.
  • Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age. Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum, where the work is on display, hails the artist's 1642 masterpiece as "the turning point in his career and as the superlative example of his creative genius.".

Sources indicate that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures. And unlike static group portraits typical of his era, the artist depicted Amsterdam's civic guards in mid-action, as they prepare to march out.

Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.

The research project "The Night Watch Lives" explores exactly that question: What kinds of life forms inhabit the surface of the famous painting?

The study is a collaborative scientific and exhibition project between the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia — an Amsterdam museum dedicated to the world of microorganisms.

It's part of the broader "Operation Night Watch" restoration and research project described as the "biggest and most wide-ranging ever study and restoration of Rembrandt's most famous painting," started in 2019. Conservators and scientists in this project have been examining every aspect of Rembrandt's masterpiece using cutting-edge technology, seeking new insights into its materials, condition and history — and now, its microbiome.

The idea behind "The Night Watch Lives" was to "put microbes in a positive spotlight," Eline van Bloois, who led the research, told DW. "Honestly, if you're asking me — I'm a microbiologist, so I'm biased of course — but they really deserve more positive attention.".

Over a period of six months, van Bloois will be taking samples once a month directly from the famous painting at the Rijksmuseum, accompanied by the people working on the restoration of "The Night Watch.".

Using small sterile discs gently pressed against selected areas of the painting, the samples collect microscopic material from both varnished and unvarnished sections.

These samples are then cultivated in laboratories, allowing previously invisible microbes to grow into visible colonies that can be studied and identified.

At the "The Night Watch Lives" exhibition, visitors can view Petri dishes containing the cultivated microbial colonies. A life-size reproduction of Rembrandt's masterpiece also demonstrates where the samples were taken, and which microorganisms were found there.

It has been revealed that at the exhibition's opening on November 11, the installation included the findings of two of van Bloois' sampling sessions. Four more will be added over the coming months, allowing the museum's visitors to follow the results of the study as it unfolds.

In a recent development, that means the exhibition's visitors "will be figuring out what I've found as I'm figuring it out myself," explains the microbiologist. "We really take them through that journey with us.".

People often fear microbes or associate them with disease, even though the vast majority of these microscopic organisms are actually harmless or vital to human survival.

Some of the organisms found on the painting "are very commonly found on human skin, for instance, and they're a healthy part of the microbiome; most humans actually have these bacteria with them," says van Bloois, adding that the presence of these microbes on the painting made sense, since humans are often near the work.

But another bacterium stood out in the samples: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a species first identified at a sugar refinery in Japan in 2013. How this microorganism ended up on the Dutch "Night Watch," or when, is a guessing game.

In a recent development, "It's part of the fun and part of the frustration in microbiology. You cannot ask the microbes where they originate from," says van Bloois. "It would make our lives a bit easier, but it's also fun to have a little bit of a mystery.".

The samples also revealed bacteria from soil, often found in plant roots. Could these organisms somehow harm the painting? Could plants start growing on the work?

Van Bloois explains why this is highly unlikely: On the painting, the bacteria can form inactive spores, but for the study, the researcher "provided them with all the nutrients and the right temperature and the right humidity that allowed them to grow again.".

Still, studying these organisms may eventually contribute to understanding how paintings age, how environmental conditions affect cultural heritage, and how museums can better preserve priceless works of art.

As to whether the microorganisms could date back to Rembrandt's time, the microbiologist states that's also "highly unlikely" — but here again, microbes cannot reveal their origin story.

As part of the larger "Operation Night Watch" team, van Bloois is definitely inspired by this "group effort where everyone is just really enthusiastic about telling these stories and adding to the knowledge surrounding 'The Night Watch.'".

The microbiological samples revealed by the laboratory process resemble abstract art in miniature: colorful clusters, delicate textures and intricate patterns created by living organisms.

And as the study is unfolding publicly, it also feels like an artistic performance of its own.

The project also perfectly embodies the full name of the museum where the exhibition is held: Natura Artis Magistra, a Latin phrase that translates to "nature is the teacher of art and science," as the microbiologist points out: "It's really cool to see science and art all come together in this project.".

The exhibition "The Night Watch Lives" runs at ARTIS-Micropia in Amsterdam until the end of May 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when you think you're going to settle in for a long winter's nap, there's more high-stakes women's soccer to watch. The 2026 Concacaf W Championship paves the way to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2028 Summer Olympics, and eight national teams from the region will play a knockout bracket starting Friday, Nov. 27.

With World Cup and Olympic berths decided along the way, fans can watch all of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship on CBS Sports Golazo Network and Paramount+.

Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament:.

All times Eastern -- all games will air on Paramount+.

Friday, Nov. 27 (quarterfinals).

Saturday, Nov. 28 (quarterfinals).

It has been revealed that saturday, Dec. 5 (third-place match and final).

The Concacaf W Championship is a senior women's national team championship tournament that doubles as the region's qualifier for both the World Cup and the Olympics.

This year's edition has a new format that sends teams to the 2027 World Cup and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The biggest change is the quarterfinal bracket. The top two ranked teams, the United States and Canada, earned byes into the tournament. Jamaica, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama, Haiti, and El Salvador all earned spots through the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

Back in 2022, eight finalists were placed into two groups of four, with the top two teams in each advancing into the semifinals and clinching World Cup spots. Third-place teams were given a chance to qualify in the inter-confederation playoffs. 2022 was also the first year the competition served as both a World Cup and Olympic qualifier, but only the champion and the winner of a two-leg playoff clinched Olympic berths.

This year, the group stages are gone, and a single quarterfinal will decide who qualifies directly. In 2026, the quarterfinal winners all earn a place in the 2027 World Cup, and quarterfinal losers compete in a play-in round, with the two winners earning spots in the inter-confederation playoffs in February 2027.

The two Concacaf W Championship finalists and the third-place finisher qualify for the 2028 Summer Games. The United States are hosts of the 2028 Olympics and qualify automatically, so if they finish in the top three, the fourth-place team takes the remaining Olympic spot.

According to recent reports, the U.S. women's national team will face El Salvador for the first time in program history. El Salvador are the USWNT's first latest opponent since playing Zambia in the Olympic group stage in July 2024.

Recent findings suggest that the USWNT step into the competition as reigning Concacaf W Championship winners. They've won the last three tournaments and hold a record nine all-time titles. The USWNT won all five of their games in the 2022 W Championship without conceding a goal and outscored opponents 13-0. The USWNT are 106W-1D-0L in matches against teams ranked outside of FIFA's Top 25, drawing only to Costa Rica 0-0 in July 2024 in Washington, D.C.

Industry observers note that manager Emma Hayes named a 23-player roster for the tournament, but recently made some changes following the 2026 NWSL Championship. Trinity Rodman, who sustained a shoulder injury, has been replaced by Jaedyn Shaw, and Shaw will be replaced by Lia Godfrey on the U-23 roster.

Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse was also ruled out of the U-23 roster and is replaced by Denver Summit FC defender Natalie Means.

El Salvador have never qualified for a Women's World Cup and will make their debut at the Concacaf W Championship. They qualified for the tournament by winning Group F with three clean sheets against Honduras, Barbados, and Trinidad & Tobago.

Head coach Eric Acuna is still leading the group after previous investigations into alleged abusive conduct,  and he publicly criticized players just last month after losses to Paraguay.

Players are trying to move forward and are led by Brenda Ceren, who led the team with five goals, followed by Danielle Fuentes with four, during the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

Newcastle are being tipped to solve their goalscoring issues this winter with a move to bring Ivan Toney back to St James’ Park.

It is a transfer which would reunite the England international with former boss Matthias Jaissle, with whom he worked at current club Al-Ahli.

Finding the back of the net has proved a major headache for Jaissle since taking the reins on Tyneside and following a summer exodus that stripped the Magpies of their spine, none of Newcastle’s current central striking options have managed to nail down a starting spot in his team.

Recent findings suggest that will Osula and Yoane Wissa have mustered just a single league goal apiece so far this campaign, while Matias Fernandez-Pardo is still waiting to open his account. Without a reliable penalty-box presence, Jaissle’s side have lacked a cutting edge in the final third.

Toney thrived under Jaissle during their time together in Saudi Arabia. The former Brentford frontman has been expectedly prolific in the Middle East, netting 87 times in 110 appearances across all competitions.

Any transfer negotiations may even be smoothed over by shared ownership links, as both Al-Ahli and Newcastle are majority-owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Despite his form in the Saudi Pro League, Toney has slipped down the international pecking order and missed out on recent England squads, a setback that is expected to spark a push for a Premier League return in the Latest Year.

A clip of Jude Bellingham standing up for a female reporter who was interrupted during a post-match interview has gone viral.

BBC Sport’s Spanish football reporter Elizabeth Conway attempted to ask Bellingham a follow-up question in the mixed zone - where media gather to interview players - after asking him about his second-half goal in Real Madrid’s 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

Her second question was interrupted by a male reporter, leading Bellingham to say, “Sorry, she's got one more”, before answering Conway’s follow-up.

The clip of the interview spread widely on social media after the Champions League game, which meant Real Madrid - who had gone 1-0 down in the first half before storming back - extended their 100% winning record in this season’s league phase.

Conway told BBC Radio WM the mixed zone is “utter carnage” and can be “intimidating” as one of few women working in sports media, saying: “You've got elbows you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.

“I'm one of very, very, few female reporters and one of very, very, few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so notable.”.

Of Bellingham’s interjection, she said: “It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.”.

The 23-year-old was widely praised on social media for how he handled the situation, with comments reading “A whole lot of class” and “a role model for young men”.

Bellingham scored in the 60th minute and provided the assist for Vinicius Junior’s late goal, with Federico Valverde and Kylian Mbappe, who scored a brace, also on the scoresheet.

The England star was part of a triple change at half-time and made an immediate impact, with his inventive goal coming from a touch with his left foot before he chipped it up with his right and volleyed home from 25 yards.

Real Madrid top the group stage standings after five games played.

#152539. Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1097 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year.
  • A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland.
  • Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

Words by Saugat Bolakhe and photos by CJ Karki.

A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland. Beneath a canopy of pines, Himalayan chestnuts and Nepalese alders, the group listens as wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal guides them through a questionnaire designed to document the signs of poaching.

Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity. But instead of focusing on animals, as many conservation projects do, the group’s objective is to protect flora, specifically orchids. These flowering plants are harvested and sold across Nepal’s borders.

The flowers are prized for their ornamental value, but they are also used in traditional medicines, including Chinese, Tibetan and Ayurveda healing products.

In a recent development, multiple parts of the plant, including the stem and fruit, can also be used as ingredients. “It’s as if these plants have some magical properties about them,” Bashyal says.

Nepal has more than 500 orchid species, many of which are heavily harvested. Between 2008 and 2016, the country legally exported more than 47,000 kilograms of wild-collected orchids. However, discrepancies exist between Nepal’s export data and those of its trading partners, arising from issues such as mismatched and unreported trade amounts and species being sold under different names.

Industry observers note that the trade in animal and plant species is regulated mostly under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) agreement, which is designed to protect wildlife from exploitation. Although Nepal joined the convention more than 50 years ago, it did not introduce legislation to implement CITES until 2017.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

It has been revealed that all but two species of orchid in Nepal are now listed in CITES Appendix II, which includes species that are not currently threatened with extinction but could be if their trade is not regulated. The government must create a management initiative and a formal assessment to confirm that harvesting a species for trade won’t harm the survival of the wild population. “We haven’t prepared such a management plan for any orchid species yet. So, their trade is still considered illegal here,” Bashyal adds. Violation of the CITES Act can lead to a fine of up to 100,000 Nepalese rupees (US$660), one year in prison, or both.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

According to recent reports, bashyal first became involved in orchid research by chance. In 2018, while working on a conifer tree conservation project for non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal in Kathmandu, she visited several regional sites across the country and was often approached by people asking about the demand for orchids in the city. When her team investigated further, it realized that many people living in the villages were harvesting or actively trading the plants.

This illegal trading was often overlooked by authorities, according to Bashyal. Before suggesting a way to stop it, the team had to understand the market — specifically which species were being taken, their conservation status and how the supply chain operated. To do this, it visited orchid trading hubs across Nepal and spoke to harvesters, traders and enforcement officials.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

It has been revealed that “The local people provide information on where orchids are harvested, moved, gathered and how much they sold orchids for,” she notes. During these visits, the team shared its research and spoke about the importance of conservation, which was well received, she says. “After all, an unsustainable harvesting of the orchids severely threatens local livelihood and income,” she adds.

In a recent development, bashyal’s team at Greenhood Nepal learnt that several orchid species, including Satyrium nepalense and Pleione praecox, are harvested in large quantities for their medicinal value. Overharvesting an orchid species that is in decline can easily lead to its extinction in the wild, which makes understanding a species’ population and distribution crucial for creating sustainable harvesting practices.

After the field trips, Bashyal’s team created a series of policy briefs, drafted conservation frameworks and started the anti-poaching taskforce in collaboration with the region’s governmental forest management office to document illegal activity and conduct patrols.

The team is also developing comprehensive identification manuals and guidelines for regulators. Many existing manuals focus on identifying whole plants and flowers, but traded items can include the orchid’s thickened stem and fleshy underground storage organs, called tubers. Some orchids are boiled, or dried for several hours or days before being traded.

In some parts of Nepal, communities can earn a good income from harvesting and selling orchids alongside other medicinal plants. For many, medicinal plants are their sole source of income. “Simply telling the locals ‘you are not supposed to do this’ will not stop them from harvesting,” Bashyal notes. For this reason, imposing a blanket ban on trade might not be effective.

According to recent reports, bashyal emphasizes that tracking the wildlife trade is complex and often requires navigating delicate legal territory. Researchers must also have patience when interviewing informants. “Thus, it also comes down to following research ethics, respect and treating local knowledge as a valuable resource to build trust,” Bashyal indicates. “Only after that, can we have data and develop any intervention.”.

Germany forward Laura Freigang will miss next summer’s Women’s World Cup after accepting a suspension over failure to comply with doping regulations.

The Eintracht Frankfurt captain was accused of failing to provide a drugs test or submit her whereabouts for testing on three occasions between March 2025 and February 2026, thereby breaching the World Anti-Doping Code.

She reached an settlement agreement with WADA, Germany’s National Anti-Doping Agency, and the German football federation over the case, which has resulted in a 16-month ban backdated to 8 June 2026, the day she was notified of the case against her.

Recent findings suggest that it means she will not be eligible to return to football until 8 October 2027. She will miss the Women’s World Cup, which runs from 24 June to 25 July, in Brazil.

The 28-year-old can return to training two months before the expiry of the ban.

Eintracht Frankfurt unveiled the news on Thursday, with the club to “soon begin discussions to establish the structuring of their future contract [with Freigang] in light of this suspension”. Freigang’s contract runs until 30 June next year.

Freigang released a statement on Instagram saying: “It is crucial for me to emphasise once again that at no time was there any suspicion of doping against me.

“The last few months have been extremely hard for me. Further proceedings would have meant high financial, mental and emotional burdens for me. That's why I chose this way, in the hope of finding some calm, clarity and perspective for myself.”.

She added: “It breaks my heart not to be able to be on the field, helping my team and being able to live the everyday life that I love so much.”.

None of Eintracht Frankfurt’s results since her ban began in June are affected.

Katharina Kiel, director of women’s football, said: “The agreement that has now been reached provides clarity and planning certainty in a process that is unique to Eintracht Frankfurt – for us as a club, but above all for Laura.

“The way she and the team have handled the situation over the past few months, and the way Laura personally led by example on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the utmost recognition.

“At Eintracht Frankfurt, we have witnessed the strong sense of unity that characterises this club. We will calmly discuss the future and the details of our working relationship with Laura.”.

Freigang has 45 caps for Germany and was a member of the squad which reached the Euro 2022 final. She has been at Eintracht Frankfurt since 2018.

Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, initiatives and organizations in Germany are speaking out against planned budget cuts to the work of strengthening democracy and fighting racism and antisemitism.
  • The "Living democracy" (Demokratie Leben) program from the Ministry for Family Affairs is set to receive a total of €170 million ($187 million).
  • The draft was agreed upon by Germany's governing coalition of the conservative Union – of the Christian Democrats (CDU) and its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU) – and the center-left Social Democrats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, initiatives and organizations in Germany are speaking out against planned budget cuts to the work of strengthening democracy and fighting racism and antisemitism. Berlin is planning drastic savings measures in its draft federal budget for 2027, which is to be debated in parliament this Friday.

The "Living democracy" (Demokratie Leben) program from the Ministry for Family Affairs is set to receive a total of €170 million ($187 million). That is about €20 million less than the current year's budget allocation.

The draft was agreed upon by Germany's governing coalition of the conservative Union – of the Christian Democrats (CDU) and its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU) – and the center-left Social Democrats.

Numerous organizations consider the cuts a dire signal. Tahera Ameer from the Amadeu Antonio Foundation, a Berlin-based NGO which campaigns against right-wing extremism and discrimination, sees many initiatives in Germany under existential threat.

"In view of the antisemitic agitation, the open violence and the ever-increasing legitimization of its normalization, it is concerning that the very structures and grants which do something to oppose them are now standing on the verge of collapse," Ameer explained during a media briefing alongside other like-minded organizations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to the initiatives, the work to strengthen democratic civil society could suffer lasting damage, because long-established structures cannot simply be rebuilt after they have been destroyed.

The thing that outraged many organizations: The cuts come at a time when the extreme right is celebrating numerous election victories in Germany.

The  Alternative for Germany (AfD), parts of which are considered far-right extremist, achieved record-high results in several elections in 2026, most notably in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. "Especially in view of the AfD possibly coming into government in Saxony-Anhalt, we need these structures more urgently than ever," urged Tahera Ameer.

The promotion of democratic civil society in Germany has been controversial for years. While initiatives and associations regularly appeal for more money, some conservative politicians repeatedly criticize an alleged one-sidedness in the allocation of public funds.

It has been revealed that during the federal parliamentary debate on the funding program in March 2025, Christian Democrat politician Marvin Schulz supported the planned changes, which were put forward by German Families Minister Karin Prien, also of the CDU: "We need new areas of focus," he said. Projects working against extreme Islamism and antisemitism were underrepresented, he said.

Recent findings suggest that but initiatives to combat antisemitism will also receive less funding in the future. The Central Committee of German Catholics (ZdK) criticized cuts to the Federal Association of Departments for Research and Information on Antisemitism (RIAS), the nationwide OFEK counselling center for people affected by antisemitic violence and discrimination, and the German Alliance against Islamophobia and discrimination against Muslims, (CLAIM).

According to recent reports, the ZdK called on the German government to continue its advocacy for the protection of Jewish and Muslim life and secure this structurally and financially. They say planned cuts achieve the opposite and are a fatal signal to a diverse and democratic society.

The AfD went further in its criticism: The party called for the funding to be stopped entirely, calling the initiatives a "program for the Left to secure power for itself.".

According to recent reports, if the AfD governs in Saxony-Anhalt, it wants wide-ranging cuts. The party wants to completely abolish the renowned State Center for Civic Education and cut state funding from numerous other organizations.

In December, the AfD, which has been classified as right-wing extremist in Saxony-Anhalt, wants its lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund to be the first AfD state premier to head a state government.

According to recent reports, A spokesperson from the federal government's Family Affairs Ministry responded to questions from DW by referring to the need for the government to consolidate its budget. The goal was that funding programs "reliably continue, also in 2027, and make the biggest and widest impact possible with the means available.".

However, an alliance of several organizations does not want to give up and is calling for a complete reversal of the decision: Instead of implementing the cuts, the organizations want the government to boost the funding pool by €50 million.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Work to strengthen democracy must be funded," urged Tahera Ameer from the Amadeu Antonio Foundation. "That is a priority that we are at the moment not seeing. And that is very unsettling.".

According to recent reports, many organizations point out that the consequences of the cuts will not remain abstract. They will have very real effects on people who experience discrimination in Germany, Lina Mitschke fears. She leads the Berlin association "Each One Teach One" (EOTO), an education and empowerment organization for people of color.

"The needs haven't gone away. But from January, people coming in have nobody to properly speak with; the phone will no longer be picked up; emails will go unanswered if someone needs support," she stated.

For organizations such as EOTO, the planned cuts are a bitter setback. In past years, they had managed to raise awareness of the lived reality of Black people in Germany. "The experiences of more than a million Black people in Germany would be negated with the cuts," Mitschke noted.

The associations want to fight until the very end to reverse the decision. They say work to promote and support democracy is what holds society together.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunday’s bruising 4-0 defeat at Anfield exposed the scale of the rebuild facing Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.

For all the scrutiny aimed at Man United’s midfield and attack, it is the fragility at the back that is of greatest concern - the club have now conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's top five leagues this season.

With the January transfer window fast approaching, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey - often linked with an Old Trafford move - is rapidly playing himself into contention for a switch.

It has been revealed that man United’s need for centre-half reinforcements could hardly be more urgent after the weekend's display. Matthijs de Ligt looked worryingly off the pace against Liverpool, struggling with his turning circle and repeatedly caught out whenever Andoni Iraola's side broke at speed.

According to recent reports, the long-term picture looks increasingly bleak, too. Lisandro Martinez is widely expected to move on at the end of the season after previously speaking out publicly against the club, leaving a left-footed vacancy at the heart of defence.

Industry observers note that across the rest of Pochettino’s central defensive options, there is a lack of ready-made solutions. Leny Yoro, who endured a miserable afternoon of his own on Merseyside, and Ayden Heaven are both still very junior in their development, while Harry Maguire isn't getting any younger.

Throwing teenagers and early-20-somethings into an Old Trafford pressure cooker every week is no recipe for climbing the table, nor can Man United rely indefinitely on an ageing veteran to bail them out, as Maguire has done so consistently in the past.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That is why Bassey ticks so many boxes for Man United’s new era under Pochettino.

Turning 27 on New Year’s Eve, the Nigeria international is entering his prime years as a defender. And having racked up more than 100 Premier League appearances since arriving in west London from Ajax in 2023, he brings the sort of battle-hardened top-flight pedigree Man United are crying out for.

In doing so, he removes the adaptation risk that has plagued so many overseas Old Trafford arrivals. His commanding display in Fulham’s 1-1 draw away at Manchester City on Saturday makes the appeal obvious; Bassey has good recovery pace, is dominant in physical duels, and comfortable defending wide channels.

Bassey won't cost the earth either as his initial four-year contract at Craven Cottage expires next summer, and although Fulham hold an option to extend his stay by a further 12 months, his contractual situation keeps any potential fee firmly within reach for a club of Man United's stature and commercial acumen.

Fulham are understandably eager to tie him down to fresh terms, but the lure of spearheading Pochettino’s Old Trafford reboot may prove hard to resist.

In FourFourTwo's view, if Bassey maintains his current level over the coming weeks, don't rule out a January approach.

Tosin Adarabioyo: ‘No one can chat s*** about Cole Palmer’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Tosin Adarabioyo has leapt to the defence of former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer amid criticism of the Englishman’s attitude.
  • Palmer came under fire for a viral interaction with Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s bruising 4-1 thrashing by Leeds last weekend, brushing off the Brazilian after opting not to acknowledge the home fans who booed the team at full-time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Tosin Adarabioyo has leapt to the defence of former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer amid criticism of the Englishman’s attitude.

Palmer came under fire for a viral interaction with Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s bruising 4-1 thrashing by Leeds last weekend, brushing off the Brazilian after opting not to acknowledge the home fans who booed the team at full-time.

The 24-year-old is going through a difficult patch at the moment, having been left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad again for the November internationals after the German manager claimed “he misses too opportunities to impress”.

This led to questions over Palmer’s commitment to the England cause, something club team-mate Morgan Rogers emphatically refuted as “nonsense” and “a lie”.

And Tosin, who moved to from Chelsea to rivals Tottenham in the summer, has now become the latest to publicly back Palmer, with whom he shared two seasons at Stamford Bridge.

“No one can chat s*** about Cole,” Tosin noted.

It has been revealed that “For me, he's one of the best players I've ever seen. You can say what you want. Honestly, you guys can say what you want. He's a top level player. He will continue to get better.”.

Asked whether he was surprised about Palmer’s omission from the England squad, he replied: “Yeah, for sure. Of course, I'm surprised. For me, he's the best No 10 in the Premier League.”.

Tosin also echoed Rogers’ sentiment in regards to doubts over Palmer’s hunger to play for the Three Lions, with the Chelsea forward struggling to get back in favour with Tuchel after missing out on the World Cup, before his return to the international fold in September was swiftly curtailed by injury.

“False, false, false,” Tosin added. “I know Cole's dreams, his aspirations. So, yeah, it's completely false.”.

While Tosin will passionately defend Palmer against his critics, this doesn’t spare the Chelsea man of a friendly jibe, especially in the wake of Tottenham’s first win at Stamford Bridge in eight years last month.

Palmer was sent off in the 2-0 defeat to their fierce rivals and Tosin, who missed the match through injury, was sure to savour the triumph at his mate’s expense.

It has been revealed that asked if the pair shared some post-match banter, Tosin laughed: “Cole's my guy, man - yeah, of course. But I'll keep that secret.”.

Palmer was among a number of Tosin’s team-mates, past and present, supporting him at the launch of his trading card shop, Card Cop, in London. The retail space in Borough Yards will open to the public on Thursday 26 November.

The Spurs defender, who is an avid collector, is joined by the likes of former Blues team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill, as well as West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, in investing in the business.

Along with the investors, Chelsea’s contingent at the launch party included Rogers, Emmanuel Emegha and Jamie Gittens, while the likes of Dominic Solanke, Micky van de Ven, Archie Gray and Ben Davies came down to support their relatively new Spurs colleague.

Sources indicate that “It’s a testament to what we're like as a team,” Tosin said. “We're all very close and very supportive of each other. The boys didn't have to turn up today, but they did. It's amazing. I'm very thankful to them.”.

After a dire start to the season, feeling the hangover of their near-miss with relegation last term, Spurs have finally found their groove under Roberto De Zerbi and are now just one point off Chelsea after four wins in five.

Tosin puts the uptick in form down to the team’s Marbella training camp during the first international break of the season, which was crucial in forming a bond within the team.

“It's our trip to Marbella,” he noted. “We had a great time. We bonded together. We learned a lot about each other, and we're all striving to put this club where we think it belongs.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethan Nwaneri's Arsenal career appears to be floundering, with the on-loan Borussia Dortmund teenager facing a further transfer setback.

Nwaneri returns to his parent club tonight in the Champions League with the Bundesliga giants and is eligible to face Arsenal despite still being owned by the Gunners.

But beyond this campaign, his future remains uncertain, with manager Mikel Arteta even recently alluding to the teenager's struggles at Signal Iduna Park.

Nwaneri became the Premier League's youngest-ever player in 2022 at the age of 15 – with Max Dowman later taking that record – before establishing himself in the 2024/25 season as a serious option on the right wing for the Gunners.

But after going out on loan at Marseille last term and heading to Dortmund this time, the teenager is yet to impress, with Arteta even admitting this week that “moments are not enough” for Nwaneri in his development and that consistency must follow.

A report from Sport Witness, likewise, reads as bad news for the 19-year-old, with the Gunners now pursuing a move for Gilberto Mora as soon as January.

Mora was the youngest player selected for the 2026 World Cup and has impressed hugely in his native Mexico, courting the attention of virtually every big club in Europe.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In attacking midfield areas, Arsenal already have the likes of Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Max Dowman – with the latter two options on the wing – and should Arsenal bring in another teenage talent, Nwaneri's first-team opportunities would appear even scarcer.

FourFourTwo understands that the Gunners were open to offers for the starlet over the summer, opting to retain him and develop him at one of the best finishing schools in European football, though the paths of Nwaneri and Hale End colleague Myles Lewis-Skelly have been drastically different, thanks, in part, due to competition for places.

With Liverpool also circling for Mora, however, the Gunners may well have to present a particularly enticing package to secure the 18-year-old.

According to the report, the youngster has a release clause of around €25 million, making any move for him particularly costly – and suggesting that the Gunners could well incorporate him into their first team immediately.

Nwaneri, meanwhile, is valued by Transfermarkt at €25m. Arsenal return to Champions League action tonight against Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 06:19 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 27 November 2026.

Manchester United will launch a newly introduced matchday mental health and suicide prevention initiative at Saturday’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford.

Working with the Premier League and Talk About It Mate, a support group based in Salford, United will host 10 sessions of The Check-In this season aimed at providing a welcoming space where supporters can drop in to talk with trained counsellors and volunteers.

Rhys Bennett, who was the captain of United's last FA Youth Cup-winning team in 2022, has spoken about the benefits of a recent Talk About It Mate session at Salford Lads Club. Bennett’s father David tragically took his own life last year.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s probably the most powerful thing I’ve ever done,’ said Bennett. ‘I’ve never done anything like this before. It’s made me feel even better than I did when I came in the door two hours ago. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it.

According to recent reports, ‘My dad passed at 51 and I think he grew up in the, “you’ll be alright, just crack on” (generation). He was an honest working man, and he went about his daily business until it became too much for him.

Industry observers note that ‘For him it would have been a really crucial thing to get things off his chest. A judgement free zone. It would have helped him massively. People are sharing the same experiences, people sat in a circle all going through different things.

Manchester United will launch a newly introduced matchday mental health and suicide prevention initiative at Saturday’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford.

Rhys Bennett (right), who was the captain of United's last FA Youth Cup-winning team in 2022, attended a recent Talk About It Mate session at Salford Lads Club.

‘To be honest, I was a little bit nervous. I'm not a nervous kind of person, but I think within five minutes, it's just no judgment and having that full confidence in being able to talk about how I'm really feeling.

‘I'm coming up for a year of my dad's passing. My dad committed suicide, and I played football for a living. I think it's hard navigating through being in a high-pressure environment.

Industry observers note that ‘I think it is the judgment thing, and not wanting to burden other people. But I think it's so key that you realise that most of the time it's not a burden.’.

In a recent development, bennett, who made a permanent move to Fleetwood in the summer and played in the League Two club’s shock Carabao Cup win over Arsenal last month, added: ‘You put the brave face on, and I feel weaker. But the more I talk about it, and the more I let my emotions out, that definitely does make me stronger in day-to-day life.

‘I used to just shut it out because I'm rocking up on a Saturday and a Tuesday in front of fans, and I've got to perform, and I feel everything. You get the adrenaline and everything of a football match, and then I'm back down to square one.

Industry observers note that ‘Just how open everyone was and how open I could be myself, really did surprise me. There wasn’t at any point that I couldn’t share something I was feeling. Everything came from the heart, it was really authentic and really powerful.’.

Running five weekly men’s groups across Salford and with more than 1,000 group sessions delivered, Talk About It Mate creates spaces where men can connect, share experiences and support one another.

With a community-led approach to improving mental health and well-being, the organisation helps men build connections and reduce isolation.

United will host 10 sessions of The Check-In this season aimed at providing a welcoming space where supporters can drop in to talk with trained counsellors and volunteers.

Bennett, whose father David tragically took his own life last year, spoke about how the session gave him 'full confidence in being able to talk about how I'm really feeling'.

Man United say their partnership with Talk About It Mate will provide a welcoming space where supporters can access help on matchdays.

Mike Richard, founder of Talk About It Mate, mentioned: ‘We've spent years creating spaces where men feel safe enough to open up, and we're proud to be working with Manchester United to bring that approach to supporters.

‘Football has an incredible ability to bring people together, but being surrounded by thousands of people doesn't necessarily mean you feel connected. We know that some of the most important conversations can start in ordinary, familiar places – that's the kind of environment we want to create at Old Trafford.

Sources indicate that ‘This isn't about waiting until someone reaches crisis point. It's about making conversations around mental health a normal part of everyday life.’.

According to The Samaritans, 5,738 suicides were registered in England in 2025, which equates to 11.1 deaths per 100,000 people.

The male suicide rate was 17.2 per 100,000 – compared to 5.4 per cent among females – with men aged 50-54 having the highest rate of any population group.

Rachel Fraser, United’s internal communications and inclusion director, remarked: ‘Our fans give so much to this club, and ensuring they feel supported in return is incredibly important to us.

‘Through our partnership with Talk About It Mate, we are proud to provide a welcoming space where supporters can access help on matchdays.

It has been revealed that ‘Football creates friendships and communities for fans that span generations. The Check-In builds on that sense of connection and seamlessly fits into the matchday routine, providing a safe and accessible space for those needing support.’.

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

Six months after the glory of that Europa League final, Aston Villa’s return to Istanbul proved a chastening night of disappointment.

Unai Emery’s team have undergone a significant rebuild since that stirring night in May and this was another occasion where Villa 2.0 were exposed as a work in progress.

Emery’s run without a win has extended to six matches in all competitions and Villa’s Champions League campaign does not promise to get any easier, with Paris St-Germain up next.

There was always likely to be a period of transition this season, as six of the heroes from the Europa League final’s starting XI were sold over the summer.

Despite some encouraging signs before the last international break, and three successive Champions League wins, Villa are now enduring a difficult run.

Their second-half performance in particular was poor, and Galatasaray secured victory with the evening’s first shot on target.
